home_content_block_body:
Gardens in Southampton vary enormously. Compact terraced back gardens in Portswood sit at one end of the scale. Bassett Heath sits at the other, with large detached plots, some close to a quarter acre. Mature trees shape how a garden can be laid out, and long plots with established planting mean structural decisions carry more weight than in a smaller suburban garden.

Portswood's conservation area brings a different set of considerations. The Edwardian frontages on roads like Brookvale Road are generous, but paving and fencing changes to front gardens face conservation area and Article 4 controls. Getting the planning right before any ground is broken saves trouble later. Those layout decisions matter more than they might in a standard residential street.

We're a family run team of four. Our [gardener](/gardener/) work covers lawns, hedges, borders and fencing. [Landscape gardener](/landscape-gardener/) projects run from new patios and paths through to full garden redesigns. The [landscape designer](/landscape-designer/) service is for homeowners who want a clear plan before anything is agreed. And our [lawn care service](/lawn-care-service/) is there when the grass itself needs proper attention rather than just a cut.

One concern we hear often is about groundwork that fails later. Every job we price accounts for what is actually underneath: the levels, the drainage and the access, before a figure goes anywhere near a customer.

We work across [landscaping in Romsey](/locations/romsey/), [landscaping in Winchester](/locations/winchester/) and [landscaping in Eastleigh](/locations/eastleigh/), and the villages in between. Call us on [CV: phone] if you want to check whether we cover your area.

faq_answer (How much does landscaping cost in Southampton?):
Landscaping costs vary depending on the size of the job, the type of work and the ground conditions. A larger plot in Bassett Heath with mature trees is a different undertaking to a compact back garden. Bigger projects with drainage or levelling involved add groundwork that isn't always obvious until we visit. We put the full cost in writing before anything starts.

faq_answer (Is it better to lay turf or sow grass seed?):
Turf gives you a usable lawn sooner; seed costs less and suits larger areas. Both need the right timing. Spring and early autumn are the right windows in Southampton, when the ground is warm enough to encourage establishment. For larger gardens, seed is often the practical choice; if you need the lawn in use quickly, turf gets you there faster. We'll advise when we visit.

faq_answer (What happens if something isn't right after the job?):
If something isn't right, call us and we'll come back to look at it. Every job we carry out is done to the standard of reasonable care and skill all trades are required to meet. We'd rather put something right than leave you with a problem, so raise it with us directly on [CV: phone] as soon as you notice it.

faq_answer (How soon can you start?):
For most jobs, we can get started the same week. Larger projects take longer to book in. Full garden redesigns, significant paving or drainage work all need a confirmed start date agreed at quote stage. We'll set that with you before anything is scheduled.

Yes, the quote is completely free and there's no obligation to go ahead. We'll look at the garden and give you a price for what we've discussed. If you decide not to proceed, that's fine.

faq_answer (How long does a garden landscaping project take?):
It depends on the size, the groundwork involved and which materials are needed. A patio on a straightforward garden differs from a larger project with drainage, new levels and planting. Weather can shift hard landscaping days if ground conditions change. We'll give you a realistic timescale when we price the job and let you know if anything changes it.

faq_answer (Why does water sit on my patio or lawn after rain?):
Persistent wet patches usually have one of three causes: the ground beneath may drain slowly, a paved surface may fall the wrong way and pool water rather than shed it, or there is simply nowhere for the water to go once it reaches the lowest point. Southampton's soils vary, and some investigated sites show seasonally waterlogged conditions. We look at all three before recommending any drainage or paving work.
